note: Workloads are 'user task' evaluation conditions (decision-method.md section 1.1, objective AGG-S): results are never averaged across workloads. File selection uses only the archive's own manifest (entry paths, kinds, sizes) and the declared seed; it never reads corpus statistics. 'Regular file' means an Entry whose data is File with internal content.
seed_rule: Every workload seed is derived as SHA-256('EXP-REMOTE-002/' + workload_id + '/' + item_id + '/' + str(spec seeds.command)) truncated to 64 bits, so candidates and repetitions see identical file selections.
session_rule: A session is one open_indexed_random (or open_indexed_random_encrypted) call with a fresh RangeSession; 'cold' means no state carried from earlier sessions except where a candidate explicitly defines a persistent cache.

WL-OPEN.note: Also the list/inspect cost: remote list reads no data beyond open in the status quo (docs/random-access-v1.md, Reports and trace)

operations: read_entry(first regular file in manifest path order)

WL-RAND1.sessions: S = min(32, regular file count); each session is cold
operations: read_entry(one file drawn uniformly without replacement across sessions)
WL-RAND1.aggregation_within_item: median over sessions (and p95 reported when S >= 20)

operations: K x read_entry(files uniform without replacement; K capped at the regular file count)
1024 x read_entry(with replacement; Zipf exponent 1.0 over a seeded permutation of regular files)
read_entry for every regular file under directory D in path order
WL-SUBTREE.directory_rule: D = the non-root directory with the largest number of descendant regular files among directories with at most 4096 descendant regular files; ties by smallest path bytes. If the archive has no such directory, the first min(4096, n) regular files in path order.

operations: read_entry(largest regular file; ties by path)
for the largest regular file of at least 4 MiB: 16 seeded byte ranges per stratum, strata {1 B, 4096 B, 1048576 B} (decision-method T-22), plus the whole entry as the fourth stratum
WL-RANGE.status_quo_semantics: the production API has no sub-object range read, so each range costs one verified read_entry of the whole object followed by an in-memory slice; candidates with sub-object reads define their own request plans
WL-RANGE.applicability: a regular file of at least 4 MiB

operations: read_entry for every regular file ordered by the physical offset of its first Chunk frame
read_entry for files taken from a seeded permutation until cumulative logical bytes >= f x total regular-file logical bytes
GET the whole archive (status quo client cannot; modelled as one 200 response, or as consecutive 64 MiB ranges for range-only origins)
local full verify (CPU measured in EXP-REMOTE-005)

sources.memory: MemoryRandomReadSource wrapped in a recording source that logs every read_exact_at and revision call (revision calls are counted as HEAD requests for the HTTP projection)
sources.http-loopback: HttpRangeSource against ebr-origin on 127.0.0.1 with no proxy; origin log gives exact HTTP requests, statuses, body and header bytes
sources.http-emulated: HttpRangeSource through ebr-netem-proxy at a calibrated profile (EXP-REMOTE-001)
sources.local-file: LocalFileRandomReadSource (reference for OD-10 local metrics; page cache state recorded)
